title: ForgeLink Product Identity and Communications Platform Narrative

preflight.note: Created before repo-wide ForgeLink product-definition, public narrative, diagram, UI-copy, MCP-context, or documentation alignment begins.

acceptance_criteria.text: Establish one canonical ForgeLink product-definition authority whose semantics state that ForgeLink is a local-first communications, coordination, and human-authority platform for people, agents, and applications, with direct human operation as a first-class path and governed programmatic integration as an additional path.

Document direct human-operated ForgeLink workflows as first-class product behavior that does not require ForgeWire, Fabric, MCP, an agent runtime, or an LLM, while preserving human authority/governance as a core ForgeLink differentiator.

Perform and preserve a repository-wide narrative inventory of product-defining language, classifying occurrences as stale product-level framing, correct subsystem framing, immutable historical context, unrelated technical-boundary language, or ambiguous material requiring explicit review; do not use mechanical global replacement.

Reconcile the root README so its introduction, What ForgeLink Is/Is Not sections, architecture, current product surface, standalone-use language, and integration sections consistently present humans as users of ForgeLink rather than merely endpoints for agents, without claiming unshipped capabilities.

Reconcile docs/public-narrative.md and other current public-facing product narrative so ForgeLink is not defined solely as Human-Boundary Infrastructure or as the place where a system asks and a human decides; communications, coordination, direct human operation, agent/application participation, and human authority must all remain visible.

Update product-level architecture diagrams and captions to represent the human cockpit, communication domains/provider edges, people/contacts, policy/authority/audit, and optional agent/application API/MCP integration; narrow agent-to-human diagrams remain permitted when they explicitly document only that subsystem or use case.

Audit and align MCP persona/resources/documentation so forgelink-human can remain accurately described as an agent-facing human bridge while no MCP text accidentally defines the entire ForgeLink product as only that bridge; do not rename the MCP package solely for narrative aesthetics.

Audit current communications runtime, provider, messaging, voice, contacts, notifications, firewall/consent, data-safety, Tauri/mobile, and related docs for material product-identity drift, clearly distinguishing human-operated, agent/application-originated, shared, provider-specific, local-only, current, and planned behavior where relevant.

Audit material operator-cockpit, onboarding, settings, help, and shared Tauri/mobile UI copy so ordinary communications operation remains understandable without assuming the user is supervising an agent; any functional navigation redesign discovered as necessary must be separately justified rather than hidden inside copy work.

State explicitly in current product documentation that ForgeWire/Fabric compatibility is optional integration, not a ForgeLink runtime prerequisite; ForgeWire/Fabric must not become the assumed owner of ordinary ForgeLink communication state, provider credentials, or human-operated workflows.

Coordinate WI041 fax documentation with the canonical ForgeLink product definition without making WI041 depend on WI042 and without describing fax as shipped until WI041 implementation and acceptance evidence prove it.

Preserve completed work items, evidence, decision records, and historically accurate reports rather than rewriting history for modern terminology; add links or narrow clarifications only where current-reader confusion would otherwise be material.

Establish future authoring guidance or a narrowly scoped validation/review guardrail ensuring no current product-level document defines the entire ForgeLink product solely as an agent/system/application reaching a human, while avoiding brittle checks that reject legitimate subsystem, security, ingress, or trust-boundary language.

Preserve documentation truthfulness by distinguishing shipped/current, active implementation, proposed/planned, and conceptual/future capabilities across all updated narrative; broader product positioning must not inflate fax, Tauri/mobile, provider, or other roadmap maturity.

Run applicable RepoPact, documentation/link/build, diagram/render, and UI-copy validation and capture durable evidence showing semantic consistency across the root README, canonical product definition, public narrative, major diagrams, and MCP persona/resources.
